maya: quick one — seeing nondeterministic MRR/ndcg numbers when we run the int8 reranker smoke eval across different seeds. anyone else?
jordan: yep, reproduced. seed=42 -> MRR@10 0.327, seed=7 -> 0.314. same candidate pools, same eval harness.
nehir: how big is the variance across runs? that’s kinda large. are you shuffling candidates or queries differently?
maya: it's stable for fp16 (0.336) but int8 bounces. ndcg@10: fp16 0.412, int8 run A 0.395, run B 0.382. we run PTQ with the usual calibration set.
sam: two quick suspects: 1) kernel non-determinism in the quant runtime (fused ops), 2) tokenization differences from trailing whitespace / html in queries that interact weirdly with quantized scoring.
jordan: good call. I dug logs: sometimes top-1 score ties and we break ties by argmax indeterminate ordering in the embedding vector dot product when floats get quantized. small changes flip ordering.
nehir: can you paste the eval command?
jordan: sure:
```
python eval_rerank.py --model /models/rerank-v3-int8 --cands path/to/candidates.jsonl --queries path/to/queries.jsonl --seed 42 --batch-size 128 --metric mrr ndcg@10 --write-outputs /tmp/out.jsonl
```
maya: I also saw cases where the runtime wasn't zeroing KV cache between requests in the local harness — that could leak across examples and be stochastic depending on batching order.
sam: ops note: for fused matmul kernels on older cu libs, we sometimes get different FP32 accumulation orders — that explains quant nondet. Have we tried `REDWOOD_FORCE_DETERMINISTIC=1` in the runtime?
maya: tried that — it reduces but doesn't eliminate diffs (MRR delta drops to ~0.004).
nehir: next steps: 1) add deterministic reduce flag + reproducible thread pool scheduling, 2) canonicalize query/doc formatting (strip html, normalize whitespace) before tokenization, 3) run N=10 seeds and report mean+std. also add tie-breaker deterministic fallback (stable sort by doc id).
jordan: will add a small change to eval harness: `--normalize-queries` that runs `html.unescape` + `re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()` pre-tokenize.
maya: also worth checking calibration data ordering for PTQ — if it samples different batches across runs that could affect quant scales. pin the calibration RNG.
sam: I'll open infra ticket to pin blas/fft libs on the CI runners to the deterministic image for quant smoke tests.
ci-bot: job rerank-quant-smoke #142 kicked by jordan — results -> https://ci.redwood.ai/job/142 (will post artifacts).
maya: thanks. after fixes let's run across three datasets (webQA, support-logs, internal-faq) and compare mean ndcg/mrr with std. if still big variance we probably need QAT or fallback to fp16 for critical slices. :thumbsup:
